  "hypotheses": [
    {
      "explanation":"synthetic_identity",
      "likelihood":"medium",
      "reasoning":"Shared-address linkage and failed identity verification are consistent with an account operated under an identity the customer cannot verify. The packet does not establish which component of the check failed."
    },
    {
      "explanation":"stolen_card",
      "likelihood":"medium",
      "reasoning":"Failed issuer authentication could indicate unauthorized card use, although the packet supplies no country mismatch or processor-decline history."
    },
    {
      "explanation":"household",
      "likelihood":"low",
      "reasoning":"Shipping to a shared home plausibly explains the address linkage. However, the home registration does not qualify for the household exception, and household sharing does not resolve the failed identity check."
    }
  ],
  "disposition":"escalate",
  "citations":["R08","FP-2 §6.3","FP-2 §6.4(b)","FP-2 §6.6(b)","FP-2 §5.2","FP-2 §5.3(b)","FP-2 §5.1(b)","FP-2 §4.2","FP-2 §2.5"],
  "next_check":"none",
  "memo":"Only R08 holds, establishing Linkage. The shared address is the account's home, but its registration is too recent for the household exception. No earlier outcome settles the order. Row §6.6(b) initially required id_check; its completed failure now decides the disposition under §5.3(b). Recommend the standard escalation because Linkage remains present; decline is also permitted. The order is unshipped, so escalation voids and refunds it and blocks the account and policy-defined linked accounts. Household sharing is the strongest benign explanation for the address, but it does not overcome failed verification. The failure supports concern about identity or card authorization without proving a particular fraud mechanism. No further check would change the prescribed outcome."
